articles.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
articles.summary: Monitoring maritime activities is important for safety and security, particularly for detecting illegal activities, but remains challenging due to the size and complexity of the maritime domain. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is commonly used for this purpose, despite its known vulnerabilities. articles.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
articles.summary: Recent advances in speech neuroprostheses have enabled new communication avenues for people who have lost the ability to speak due to neurological illness or injury. These systems can decode neural activity during attempted speech into text by relying on language priors to achieve high decoding accuracy. articles.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
articles.summary: Robot-use agents (RUAs) have emerged as a promising approach to general-purpose robot control. However, strong performance has so far been achieved only by frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, whereas open-weight models remain substantially less capable. articles.title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations
articles.summary: Learning semantically meaningful human movement representations from 3D pose sequences is essential for human behavior modeling. Existing self-supervised methods derive supervision from artificial assumptions, e.g., invariance to augmentation within a certain range or recoverability of masked regions at a certain temporal scale, introducing heuristic hyperparameters that make the learned semantics sensitive to their settings. articles.title: Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data
articles.summary: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in non-standard late-time evolution. We investigate whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark energy density, $Ω_{\rm X}(a)$, and the gravitational response functions $μ(a)$ and $Σ(a)$. articles.summary: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. articles.title: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Image and Video Generators by Probing Activations
articles.summary: Distilling diffusion models into few-step student models substantially reduces sampling latency, but induces severe diversity collapse: samples generated from different random seeds show minimal variation. articles.title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
articles.summary: Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. articles.title: Modeling the Frictional Contact of Continuum Robots with Environments through Linear Complementarity Problem
articles.summary: Accurate friction modeling in continuum robots is essential for precise motion control and path planning. However, current approaches make predictions only for the mechanism's internal friction that is limited by the boundary forces of the Coulomb friction cone, which fail to characterize the static friction and motion hysteresis. articles.title: From smoothed analysis to backward error: The power of adaptive perturbations
articles.summary: Smoothed analysis has become a central tool in theoretical computer science, often allowing for significant improvements to worst-case running times if we settle for a solution to a small random perturbation of the problem instance. articles.summary: Generative modeling based on stochastic interpolants requires specifying two key choices: an interpolant schedule bridging the initial and target distributions, and an efficient discretization of the resulting probability-flow ODE. articles.summary: Monte Carlo neutronics analysis of tokamak designs is computationally expensive due to the complex CAD geometries required to accurately model them. articles.summary: Modern power systems are undergoing a huge shift in generation mix, including inverter-based resources that are fundamentally changing the stability dynamics of the grid. articles.summary: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) increasingly relies on a harness, the scaffold around the model that decides what it sees of its own interaction and what guidance it receives. Most existing approaches train under a hand-written harness that stays fixed throughout. articles.summary: Wigner solids and crystals are many-body phases of matter in which repulsive interactions between the charge carriers cause them to freeze into a solid. How Wigner solids compete or cooperate with integer and fractional quantum Hall liquids has been a long-standing open question. articles.title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. articles.summary: Meetings last up to an hour, and nobody knows in advance how many people will speak. Neural diarizers with a fixed number of output slots, such as Streaming Sortformer and Nemotron-3, are accurate and run online, but they cannot name more speakers than they have slots. articles.summary: Lagrangian particle tracking follows virtual particles in the velocity fields of an ocean model to study transport pathways, connectivity and dispersion. articles.summary: Wafer-scale accelerators offer massive compute capacity through hundreds of thousands of processing elements (PEs) interconnected across a single wafer, but realizing this potential requires efficient application mapping. articles.title: Pressure and Magnetic Field Control of Topology in Antiferromagnetic Bilayers
articles.summary: Controlling band topology in magnetic semiconductors requires strategies that couple electronic structure to experimentally accessible degrees of freedom. Here we propose a cooperative approach based on pressure and magnetic reorientation in A-type antiferromagnetic bilayers. articles.summary: Long-context LLMs must retain growing histories, but full attention makes each new token increasingly expensive. Inference-time learning (ITL) offers another approach. articles.title: Patient-specific Modeling of the Tricuspid Valve from 3D Transesophageal Echocardiography
articles.summary: Purpose: Image-based patient-specific simulations of the tricuspid valve (TV) could support repair planning. articles.title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
articles.summary: Detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) objects is essential for ensuring the reliability and safety of object detectors in real-world deployment. articles.summary: Physical design automation of very large-scale integrated circuits (VLSI) has made significant strides, progressing from single-stage placement and routing toward increasingly integrated full-flow implementation. articles.summary: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. articles.title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
articles.summary: This paper introduces MeReader, a privacy-preserving, offline and progress-aware AI assistant designed to function as a contextual companion for narrative reading on consumer hardware. Unlike conventional Large Language Model (LLM)-based systems that process documents/books online in an all-texts-at-once type of way, thereby risking narrative spoilers, MeReader confines both retrieval and generation to the reader's distinct position in the text. articles.summary: Boson sampling machines have become a fruitful tool for establishing new concepts, which connect fundamental physics with computer science applications. articles.summary: Audio frequency-shift keying (AFSK) is a widely adopted modulation scheme for CubeSat systems due to its favorable bandwidth efficiency and implementation simplicity. articles.summary: Common data elements (CDEs) support clinical data comparability but are usually defined manually. We investigated whether large language model agents could derive a CDE schema from sarcoma case report abstracts and apply it at scale. articles.summary: This paper documents and checks EPIGRIDS, seven open synthetic transmission grid cases from four independently built networks, made with an optimization-based construction method instead of the graph-statistics method behind most large public synthetic grids. articles.summary: Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) pose significant environmental, economic, and public-health challenges in coastal and inland water bodies, creating a need for scalable methods to collect spatially distributed water-quality data. articles.summary: Autonomous trading agents need controls that prevent problematic orders without making legitimate tasks impractical. articles.summary: Atomistic foundation models have emerged as a promising route to DFT-level accuracy for materials simulation with complex chemical environments. articles.summary: Accurately mapping the total mass distribution within galaxy clusters, including dark matter, is fundamental to understanding structure formation and constraining cosmological parameters. articles.summary: The total electron emission yield (TEEY) of dielectric surfaces may vary during electron irradiation owing to charge accumulation within the material. articles.summary: Program induction refers to the process in which a learner aims to recover a program from a few given input-output examples. articles.summary: AI-enabled remote patient monitoring is evolving beyond passive data collection toward agentic AI systems that interpret patient states, coordinate care, and initiate action across domestic and clinical settings.
